mainEntity.name: What is considered a detached living quarters?

acceptedAnswer.text: A detached living quarters is a standalone residential structure built on the same property as a primary home. Commonly referred to as a detached accessory dwelling unit, in-law cottage, or granny flat, it provides independent living space. Unlike an interior suite or attached home addition, a detached building features its own separate foundation, exterior framing, roofing, and utility connections. The intended use directly shapes the design scope. A simple guest suite may require only a bedroom, bathroom, and basic climate control, while a permanent residence for aging parents or adult children typically incorporates a complete kitchen, dedicated laundry space, and private entryways.
acceptedAnswer.description: A detached living quarters is an independent, standalone residential structure built on the same parcel as a primary home, providing private living amenities separate from the main house.
